plan.topic: Feeling dizzy or light-headed on tirzepatide: how often the US label reports dizziness (and low blood pressure) vs placebo, everyday contributors worth checking, and the signs that mean getting help
plan.angle: Calm 'Is this normal?' Short. Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer): 'Feeling dizzy when you stand up on tirzepatide? The label lists it.' The fact card should read: 'Zepbound label, two placebo-controlled weight trials pooled (adults with obesity or overweight; one trial included only people with type 2 diabetes): dizziness 4–5% on tirzepatide vs 2% on placebo; low blood pressure 1–2% vs 0%.' Copy the per-arm numbers exactly (4%/5%/4% vs 2%; 1%/1%/2% vs 0%) and present them as trial arms, never as dose steps. Add the label line: low blood pressure was more frequent in people also taking blood pressure medicines (2.2% vs 1.2%). Then: if you take blood pressure medicines, tell your prescriber about dizziness and never change them on your own. Untagged, hedged lines: eating and drinking much less can play a part; sip fluids through the day unless you've been told to limit fluids; stand up slowly. Label lines in label wording: vomiting or diarrhoea can lead to dehydration, which is linked to kidney problems; the risk of low blood sugar is higher with insulin or a sulfonylurea, plus the label's low-blood-sugar signs. Emergency card, emergency number first: 'Fainting, chest pain, or confusion: call your local emergency number right away.' Then: 'For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.' Closing (shipping 11-17 or later): 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.', then a final line that loops back to sentence 1. No subscribe line or 'link in the description'. 160 spoken words or fewer, no date words. Post note: the related-video target is the Side Effects long video. Source: Zepbound PI on DailyMed, revised 28 Aug 2026, section 6.1.
plan.why: Uncovered felt symptom that new starters search for. It fits the winning 'Is this normal?' format and avoids repeating today's pen and stomach Shorts. It rests entirely on the Zepbound PI, so it should pass the fact-check first time, and it feeds the Side Effects hub. | fact-check: Topic is safe and on-pillar (side effects, practical safety). I checked the current Zepbound label on DailyMed (revised 28 Aug 2026, https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=487cd7e7-434c-4925-99fa-aa80b1cc776b). It prints both rates for the pool of the two placebo-controlled weight-reduction trials, Study 1 and Study 2. Dizziness: placebo 2%, 5 mg 4%, 10 mg 5%, 15 mg 4%. Hypotension: placebo 0%, 5 mg 1%, 10 mg 1%, 15 mg 2%. The label also says hypotension was more frequent in people also taking blood pressure medicines (2.2% vs 1.2% without them). Two fixes are needed. (1) Population: the angle describes the pool as 'adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition'. That is incomplete, because Study 2 enrolled only people with type 2 diabetes and Study 1 excluded it. The pooled figures must say the pool combines both. (2) The blood-pressure-medicine line can now cite the label's own 2.2% vs 1.2% sentence instead of standing as an untagged tip. Keep 'never change them on your own'. The rest of the angle is acceptable: hedged everyday contributors with no tag, the label's dehydration/kidney and low-blood-sugar wording, the emergency card with the emergency number first, and the exact don't-stop line. Closing: if this ships on or after 11-17, there is no Exp F subscribe line and no 'link in the description'. End with 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.', then the emergency and don't-stop lines, then a line that loops back to sentence 1. In narration, show doses as arms only and never as a titration path. Keep the post's hashtag to #tirzepatide. Never use #Zepbound.

factcheck.summary:
This Short passes. I checked every number against the live Zepbound label on DailyMed, revised 8/2026, and they all match:
- **Dizziness:** 4%, 5% and 4% on tirzepatide vs 2% on placebo, from the table "Adverse Reactions (≥2% and Greater than Placebo) in ZEPBOUND-Treated Adults with Obesity or Overweight".
- **Low blood pressure (hypotension):** 1%, 1% and 2% vs 0%.
- **With vs without blood pressure medicines:** 2.2% vs 1.2%. This compares two groups both taking tirzepatide, and the script frames it correctly.
- **Trials:** both Studies 1 and 2 ran 72 weeks, and Study 2 enrolled only adults with type 2 diabetes.
- **Kidney injury:** the label says most cases were in people with nausea, vomiting or diarrhea leading to dehydration.
- **Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia):** the label says the risk is higher in people with diabetes who also take an insulin secretagogue (a drug that makes the pancreas release insulin, such as a sulfonylurea) or insulin.

The NIDDK page lists "dizzy, lightheaded" as low blood sugar symptoms and was last reviewed July 2021.

The spoken word count is exactly 159, within the 135–160 arm. The emergency line and the don't-stop line are copied exactly. The closing has no subscribe or link line, and the loop line works. The tips (sip fluids unless told to limit them, stand slowly) correctly carry no source tag and include the fluid-restriction caveat.

There are three minor scope and clarity fixes. Together they bring the count to exactly 160, still within the limit.

issues.claim: Low blood sugar, likelier with insulin or a sulfonylurea, can cause dizziness.
issues.problem: The narration drops the population. The label limits the higher low-blood-sugar risk to patients with diabetes taking insulin or an insulin secretagogue. The on-screen list item already says 'In diabetes', so the spoken line is broader than the card and the source.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Low blood sugar can cause dizziness. In diabetes, it's likelier with insulin or a sulfonylurea." (15 words, +3)

issues.claim: In two trials of up to seventy-two weeks
issues.problem: Both pooled studies were 72-week trials, so 'up to' is vague. Tightening the wording also frees words for the S4-6 and S4-3 fixes.
issues.fix: Replace "In two trials of up to seventy-two weeks," with "In two seventy-two-week trials," (−4 words). Change on_screen_text to: "Dizziness, 72-wk trials: 4–5% tirzepatide vs 2% placebo (adults with obesity/overweight; one trial type 2 diabetes only)"

issues.claim: Low blood pressure: one to two percent, versus zero.
issues.problem: The narration never says the zero is placebo. The stat card also leaves out the population and timeframe, which fails the muted-viewer test.
issues.fix: Narration: "Low blood pressure: one to two percent, versus zero on placebo." (+2 words). On-screen: "Low BP: 1–2% tirzepatide vs 0% placebo (same 72-wk trials)". With all three fixes the spoken count is 159 − 4 + 3 + 2 = 160, exactly at the limit.
